translation.title: Diclofenac Sodium Cataplasm (Pap)
translation.efficacy: This medicine is used for osteoarthritis, periarthritis of the shoulder, tendinitis and tenosynovitis, peritendinitis, elbow pain (tennis elbow, etc.), muscle pain, and post-traumatic swelling and pain.
translation.usage: Apply 1 cataplasm (pap) to the affected area once a day.
translation.caution: Do not use this medicine if you have experienced hypersensitivity to it, if you have or have had asthma or hypersensitivity caused by aspirin or other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics, if you are a child under 18, a pregnant woman past the fifth month of pregnancy or in the third trimester, breastfeeding, or a patient with peptic ulcer. Consult a doctor or pharmacist before use if you have bronchial asthma, if you are in the first or second trimester of pregnancy, breastfeeding or possibly pregnant, having difficulty conceiving or undergoing fertility testing, elderly, if you have or have had hypersensitivity to propylene glycol, or if you have asthma with high sulfite sensitivity. Do not use continuously for more than 2 weeks. Do not apply to skin with lesions such as exudative dermatitis, eczema, infected lesions, burns, or wounds, or to the eyes or mucous membranes. Do not use an occlusive dressing without a doctor's supervision. While using this medicine, do not apply other diclofenac products or non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs topically or use them orally. Consult a doctor or pharmacist before using together with new-quinolone antibacterials such as enoxacin; convulsions may occur. Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are using loop diuretics such as furosemide, thiazide diuretics, drugs that interfere with blood clotting such as warfarin, antiplatelet agents such as aspirin, coumarin anticoagulants, selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, or serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors. Photosensitivity reactions, swelling, skin peeling, eczema, dry skin, sometimes dermatitis, itching, redness, roughness, or irritation, rarely blistering or pigmentation, and in particular serious reactions such as contact dermatitis or anaphylactic symptoms (hives, angioedema, difficulty breathing, etc.) may occur. If any of these occur, stop use immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist. Store at room temperature away from moisture and light, and keep out of reach of children.
